featured_reviews.name: steve dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re even remotely serious about your craft, do yourself a favour and stay away from this place. This is not a professional studio, it’s a venue awkwardly pretending to be one.

We shot at Studio 3 and the constant banging noises from the neighbouring facility made it borderline unusable for any sound recording. When this was brought up to the staff, instead of resolving it, they casually pointed at a board and told us to “call the manager.” So in the middle of an active shoot, we’re expected to call someone who isn’t even on-site, only to be told in a condescending tone that it’s from an establishment called Candies next door which which has an operational kitchen as if that somehow fixes the problem.

What’s worse is the on-ground staff hovering and staring at the backdrop roll while the talent is literally mid-shot on it. In any professional studio, you get reasonable usage of the roll and pay extra if needed, you don’t get policed like you’re damaging museum property. Having staff silently stare down your talent during a take is not just unprofessional, it’s absurd.

We also shot BTS and bytes in the common couch area, which they themselves position as a usable space, only for the hiring team to get a CCTV monitoring call saying they’ll be charged for sitting on the couch because it’s a “prop.” Monitoring clients over CCTV to penalise basic usage of space is petty and ridiculous.

I’ve shot in dozens of studios, some great, some average, some difficult, but never one that felt this hostile, rigid, and poorly managed. Issues usually get solved through competent studio management. Here, the owner or manager Vicky seems fundamentally unsuited to run a studio environment.

For the price they charge, you can easily book a larger, better-equipped studio with proper sound control, basic professionalism, and staff who actually understand how shoots function. This place is a logistical headache masquerading as a studio.

featured_reviews.name: ayushi Ojha
featured_reviews.review_text:
We hired Zero Gravity Photography for our engagement shoot and trusted them with preserving memories from one of the most important milestones of our lives.

When we recently reached out regarding our engagement photographs, we were informed that the data had been permanently deleted from their Google Drive and could not be retrieved.

We were told that the team previously maintained backups but stopped doing so after Google began charging for storage. If there was a change in their backup policy, clients should have been clearly informed before permanently deleting important event data.

Unfortunately, instead of a transparent and accountable response, our experience has been marked by defensiveness. Communication has also been inconsistent, with delayed replies and periods where our messages were not responded to, which felt evasive.

Engagement photographs are not ordinary files — they are irreplaceable memories. Professional photography services must have clear data retention policies, responsible backup systems, and respectful communication.

The loss of our engagement photographs is deeply upsetting, and the handling of this situation has been extremely disappointing.

• Poor Communication: They went "radio silent" and became defensive when confronted.
• Lack of Accountability: Zero effort was made to rectify the situation or provide a transparent apology.
Engagement photos are not just "files" , they are a milestone. This company treated them as disposable overhead. Save yourself the heartbreak and hire a professional who respects the weight of your memories.

featured_reviews.name: Sheshank Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
BE VERY CAREFUL!!!!

Summary: Choose someone else. DO NOT HIRE RECALL IMAGES IF YOU WANT TO RECALL ANYTHING. His company is shut down.

Details:

We hired Rounak for our engagement ceremony on the Dec 2022. He seemed like a good and friendly person at first. He asked for advance and then the full payment post the event. He told us it was the industry norm so we obliged and handed him the entire amount.

Post this he took weeks to give us the photographs of the event. These came out well but he missed out a lot of people at the event and the number of photographs were a lot less than expected. But the quality was good. What we had realized is that he had gotten his friend along with him and he was the photographer. He was from Rikaar images, and we realized that he was the person responsible for the beautiful images in the first place. The person from Rikaar saved the event with his beautiful pictures.

We had paid Rounak (Recall Images) the full amount for even a video. He kept delaying for weeks stating one excuse or another. After 2 months he stopped replying all together. No reply to messages or to calls. He just ran away with the money. We even asked Rikaar to help us locate him but he told us Rounak was not picking up even his phone calls.

We then did more research (which we should have done before) and realized that he had done the same with others as well. And his employees were not paid. His IG is not updated and his company is more or less shut down.

My sincerest request to all of you. DO NOT HIRE RECALL. You can explore Rikaar or any other photographer. But DO NOT take recall if you want to avoid a nightmare.

Message me for proof or any other explanations.
